title: Characterizing Single-Molecule Conformational Changes Under Shear Flow with Fluorescence Microscopy
protocol: Reconstitute human plasma VWF by adding 100 µL of deionized water to 100 µg of lyophilized VWF to create a 1 mg/mL VWF stock solution.
Dialyze the VWF stock solution in 500 mL of 1x sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) for 1 hour at 4 °C with slow stirring.
Transfer 50 µL of VWF stock solution into a 0.1 mL dialysis unit with a 10,000 molecular weight cut-off and seal it with a cap.
Store the remaining VWF stock solution at -20 °C for up to 1 year.
Repeat dialysis for an additional hour using 500 mL of fresh PBS.
Prepare a 2 mM solution of NHS-PEG4-biotin by dissolving the solid in DI water immediately before the reaction.
Add 2.5 µL of 2 mM NHS-PEG4-biotin to the dialysis unit containing the VWF stock solution, resulting in a 20-fold molar excess of biotin compared to VWF monomers.
Place the dialysis unit inside a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Seal the dialysis unit with its corresponding cap.
Secure the tube-dialysis assembly with Parafilm.
Keep upright and leave at room temperature for 40 min.
Start fluorophore labeling reaction.
Prepare a 2.8 mM solution of Alexa 488 tetrafluorophenyl-ester (TFP-ester) fluorescent dye by dissolving the fluorophore solid in DI water immediately before use.
Add 2.9 µL of the 2.8 mM 488 fluorophore to the dialysis unit.
Add 2.0 µL of 1 M sodium bicarbonate to the dialysis unit.
Secure the dialysis unit in a microcentrifuge tube.
Store in the dark and leave at room temperature for 1 h and 30 min.
Place the dialysis unit in 900 mL of 1x sterile PBS.
Dialyze overnight at 4 °C.
Transfer labeled VWF into a microcentrifuge tube.
Cover the tube with aluminum foil and protect from light.
Store the VWF tube at 4 °C.
For long-term storage, add sodium azide to a final concentration of 0.02% (w/v).
Place 48 µL of 500 ng/µL lambda DNA in a PCR tube and heat for 5 min at 65 °C.
Immediately place the PCR tube on ice after heating.
Add 5 µL each of 1 mM dATP, dTTP, and dGTP to the lambda DNA mixture.
Add 4 µL of 1 mM biotin-14-dCTP to the mixture.
Add 2.5 µL of 5 U/µL Klenow Fragment (3'à5' exo-) to catalyze the DNA synthesis.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 1 h at 37 °C.
Add 1.2 µL of 0.5 M EDTA to deactivate the reaction.
Heat the reaction mixture for 5 min at 70 °C.
Remove excess nucleotides from lambda DNA using a spin column designed for 10-70 μL samples with a 6,000 molecular weight cut-off.
Place the column inside a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the column and tube at 1000 x g for 2 minutes.
Dispose of flow-through that collects in the tube.
Replace the column buffer with 500 μL of 1x reaction buffer from step 2.1.1.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 1000 x g.
Dispose of flow-through.
Repeat buffer replacement and centrifugation two more times, adding a total of 1000 μL of 1x buffer to the column.
Place the column in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Carefully add the solution from step 2.1.5 to the top layer of the column.
Centrifuge for 4 minutes at 1000 x g.
Collect the flow-through (40-70 μL) from the microcentrifuge tube and place in a PCR tube.
Label lambda DNA with fluorescent YOYO-1 dye according to standard protocols.
Prepare a solution of YOYO-1 dye and lambda DNA with a dye to base pair molar ratio of 1:10.
Assume no DNA was lost in the purification step to calculate the base pair concentration of lambda DNA.
Heat the solution for 2 hours at 50 °C in the dark to complete the reaction.
Cover the tube with aluminum foil and protect from light.
Store the covered tube at 4 °C.
Use photolithography to create microfluidic channels on a master silicon wafer according to standard protocols.
Add 5 parts silicone elastomer base to 1 part curing agent by mass in a weigh boat.
Stir the contents thoroughly for 1 min to create pre-cured PDMS solution.
Pour the PDMS solution over the wafer to create a 5 mm layer.
Cover the dish and leave it in a desiccator under vacuum for 1 h to remove air bubbles.
Incubate covered Petri dish at 60 °C overnight to cure PDMS into a flexible solid.
Cut 20 x 10 mm rectangles into the PDMS around each microfluidic channel using a razor.
Remove the rectangular PDMS blocks with tweezers.
Use a 25 G blunt end needle with sharpened edges to punch a hole 0.5 mm in diameter at one end of the channel, ensuring it goes completely through the PDMS block.
Repeat the punching process at the other end of the channel to create an inlet and outlet for flow through the channel.
Clean the surface of the PDMS block with vinyl cleanroom tape.
Blow compressed nitrogen gas over a No. 1 ½, 22 x 50 mm coverslip to remove debris.
Place the PDMS block with the channel side up and the coverslip into the chamber of a plasma bonding machine.
Start the treatment.
When treatment is complete, quickly place the PDMS block on a coverslip so that the channel is in contact with the slip.
Apply pressure along the edges of the block.
Place the coverslip-PDMS assembly on a hot plate at 115 °C for 15 min to reinforce the permanent bond.
Insert 10 cm-long, 0.25 mm inner diameter tubing into the outlet hole at the top of the PDMS block.
Inject less than 10 μL of 10 µg/mL biotinylated bovine serum albumin (BSA-biotin) dissolved in sterile 1x PBS into the inlet for VWF experiments.
Inject less than 10 μL of 1 mg/mL BSA-biotin for lambda DNA experiments.
Withhold a few microliters of BSA-biotin in the pipette tip after injection and allow the tip to remain embedded in the inlet.
Keep a droplet of DI water around the tip to prevent air bubbles from entering the channel.
Apply this technique every time a new solution is injected into the channel.
Allow BSA-biotin to incubate in the device for 2 h.
Remove the pipette tip.
Inject less than 10 μL of casein blocking solution into the channel.
Incubate for 30 minutes.
Remove the tip and inject less than 10 μL of 10 μg/mL streptavidin dissolved in sterile 1x PBS into the channel for VWF experiments.
Use 100 μg/mL streptavidin for lambda DNA experiments.
Incubate for 10 minutes.
Remove the tip and inject less than 10 μL of 1x detergent solution (0.05% Tween 20 in PBS) into the channel to wash away excess streptavidin.
Remove the tip and inject less than 10 μL of either 28.4 nM VWF diluted in casein solution or lambda DNA from step 2.3.3.
Incubate VWF for 3 minutes.
Incubate lambda DNA for 45 minutes.
Remove the tip and inject less than 10 μL of 5 mM free biotin diluted in casein solution.
Free biotin will block excess streptavidin binding sites on channel surface.
Prepare 1 mL of casein blocking solution with 2.2 mM protocatechuic acid and 37 nM protocatechuate-3,4-dioxygenase.
Load the prepared solution into a syringe and secure it in a syringe pump.
Attach one end of a 0.25 mm inner diameter tubing to the syringe needle.
Flow the solution through the tubing to remove air bubbles.
Attach the other end of the tube to the inlet of the microfluidic device.
Select the highest magnification objective (i.e., 60-100X) on a total internal reflection (TIRF) or confocal fluorescence microscope.
Add a drop of immersion oil if necessary and place the microfluidic device on the microscope stage with the coverslip flush against the objective.
Start brightfield microscopy and adjust focus until debris and bubbles are visible.
Adjust the stage in X and Y directions to position the edge of the microfluidic channel bisecting the frame.
Switch to the 488 channel (FITC).
Adjust Z-level and TIRF angle as needed to distinguish individual green, globular molecules (VWF or lambda DNA).
Adjust exposure time and laser intensity to visualize fluorescent molecules without causing photobleaching.
Adjust contrast to clearly visualize molecules.
Start flow from the syringe pump with casein blocking solution 5 minutes after step 5.6.
Use flow rates between 5,000 and 30,000 µL/h.
Stop and start flow to observe changes in molecule conformation.
Repeat process throughout various areas of the microfluidic device.
Record videos of continuous molecule behavior under shear flow.
Select optimal exposure time, frequency, and video duration to minimize photobleaching.
Save recorded videos as .AVI files with a scalebar.
Determine the length of any biomolecule under various shear rates using a customized MATLAB code.
Create a folder titled videos analysis which includes main.m, save_each_frame.m, get_length.m and get_length.fig.
Create a subfolder within videos analysis titled videos and add .AVI files to be analyzed into it.
Open main.m using MATLAB 2019a and run the code.
Type in the name of the video file to be analyzed in the command window under Please input the data file to analyze:.
Set threshold to 20 in the GUI and click on the Set threshold button to confirm.
Choose one pixel anywhere on the scale bar using the data cursor in the top tool bar.
Click Start point in the Scale bar section on the right of the window.
The (x,y) position of the chosen pixel will appear on the right of the button.
Click on the Pixel size (µm) button to measure the pixel size, which needs to be done only once per video.
Choose any pixel on the molecule of interest.
Click on Start point in the VWF section.
After the position of the chosen pixel appears on the text box on the right, click on Left end.
Click on Right end and String length to get the molecular length in the image.
